messages.author: 8cb6cad6420664b9
messages.subject: Parallel not working in bootstrapLavaan
parts:
Hi,
 
I'm having some trouble with the bootstrapLavaan function.  If I set parallel to multicore and ncpus = 20 then it takes just as long to run as without that set, and I see no spike in CPU activity in task manager, but the function does return a result (exactly the same as if I hadn't set it).  If I set parallel = "snow" then it finished quickly, and I see an appropriate spike in CPU activity, but it doesn't return my results, just an empty data.frame.  I'm using a custom function to extract the standardized path coefficients if the model converged.
 
path.coefs = function(lavaan.model) {
  if(inspect(lavaan.model, "converged")) {
    s = standardizedSolution(lavaan.model)
    r = s$est.std
    names(r) = paste(s$lhs, s$op, s$rhs)
  } else {
    r = NULL
  }
  r
}
 
I'm using lavaan v0.5-12 on windows, R version 2.15.3, Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
 
Any ideas what is going wrong?
 
Thanks

> parallel to multicore

> I'm using lavaan v0.5-12 on windows, R version 2.15.3, Platform:
> x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
> Any ideas what is going wrong?

I'm afraid parallel="multicore" is not available on Windows. That is not
a lavaan issue, but a 'Windows' issue.

In principle, parallel="snow" should work on Windows, but I have not
tested this (nor tried it) (since I work on Linux).

The bootstrapLavaan() function is modelled after the 'boot()' function
from package 'boot'. Perhaps the documentation from the boot() function
contains more information.

Yves.

parts:
The problem appears to be coming from the custom function.
 
snow works fine without FUN specified, and for a number of other types of function, but it appears that calling standardizedSolution breaks it (even if you don't use the result).
 
For example, this will not work:
 
path.coefs = function(lavaan.model) {
  s = standardizedSolution(lavaan.model)
  pi
}

res = bootstrapLavaan(sem.model, 1000, parallel = "snow", ncpus = 20, FUN = path.coefs, verbose = TRUE)
 
 
I've tried digging deeper into this, but I'm still unsure what exactly is causing this.
 
What is special about standardizedSolution that might be causing this, and is there another way to get those coefficients out?

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Parallel not working in bootstrapLavaan
parts:
On 05/01/2013 04:18 PM, mikej...@googlemail.com wrote:
> The problem appears to be coming from the custom function.
> snow works fine without FUN specified, and for a number of other types
> of function, but it appears that calling standardizedSolution breaks it
> (even if you don't use the result).

Any custom function seems to fail, eg

# this works:
bootstrapLavaan(fit, 10, parallel="snow", ncpus=3, FUN=coef

# this fails:
bootstrapLavaan(fit, 10, parallel="snow", ncpus=3,
FUN=function(x){coef(x)}, verbose=TRUE)

# this works too (on linux):
bootstrapLavaan(fit, 10, parallel="multicore", ncpus=3,
FUN=function(x){coef(x)}, verbose=TRUE)

So it seems that 'snow' doesn't like custom functions. I'm not sure why.
If you could find out, please let me know.
> and is there another way to get those coefficients out?

Yes, you can call the 'internal' function 'standardize.est.all', and it
seems to work:

bootstrapLavaan(fit, 10, parallel="snow", ncpus=3,
FUN=lavaan:::standardize.est.all, verbose=TRUE)

Yves.

On 05/03/2013 12:19 PM, Ruben Arslan wrote:
> Have you tried
>
> path.coefs =function(lavaan.model){

> require(lavaan)
> s = standardizedSolution(lavaan.model)
> pi
> }
>
>
> ?
> I remember getting problems with packages not loaded in the sub-units
> when I switched an analysis from multicore on mac to snow on windows.

YES. That's it. This works for me:

path.coefs =function(lavaan.model){
require(lavaan)
s = standardizedSolution(lavaan.model)
s$est.std
}

bootstrapLavaan(fit, R=5, ncpus=2, parallel = "snow", FUN=path.coefs,
verbose=TRUE)

Thanks for the tip!

Yves.
